content.title: About
content.content: Yogurt NFS is a fermented dairy product made by inoculating whole milk with specific bacterial cultures. It has a smooth, creamy taste with a mild tang and a velvety texture. The product is offered in various fat levels and flavor additions.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Yogurt is one of the oldest fermented milk foods, traced back to ancient Egypt.
The bacteria Lactobacillus bulgaricus and Streptococcus thermophilus used in yogurt aid digestion.
NFS yogurt is often fortified with probiotics, vitamin D and B12 to boost its nutritional profile.
In many cultures yogurt is traditionally served with honey, nuts or fresh berries.
Fermentation reduces lactose, making yogurt more tolerable for people with mild lactose intolerance.

items.title: Rich in probiotics
items.content: Live cultures support gut microbiota balance and strengthen the immune system.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Calcium in yogurt is essential for bone and teeth health.

items.title: Provides protein
items.content: Yogurt supplies high‑quality dairy protein that helps tissue repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Yogurt contains riboflavin (B2) and cobalamin (B12), important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Low‑fat options
items.content: Light versions are suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: People allergic to casein or whey may react to yogurt.

items.title: Added sugar in flavored varieties
items.content: Sweetened yogurts increase calorie intake and can contribute to tooth decay.

items.title: Live culture viability
items.content: Probiotic counts may decline if stored at high temperatures for long periods.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Yogurt NFS can be enjoyed on its own, blended into smoothies, mixed with oatmeal or granola, or used in sauces and desserts. For extra creaminess it is often combined with honey, berries or nuts.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep yogurt refrigerated at 1 °C–4 °C. After opening, consume within 3–5 days. Do not freeze, as the texture may change.
